source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text:
At the crowded line, the conveyor belt moves swiftly, the scanner clicking as items pass. Behind me stands a cart loaded with groceries, and a divider bar keeps us from touching. The cashier, engaged with a shopper, inputs each item. Another person, impatient, steps closer, causing a slight tussle for space. The register hums quietly, beeping with each scanned item. The total flashes on the screen; a prompt for loyalty-card membership. 

In the background, a digital clock ticks away, marking time. The shopper ahead adjusts the bagging area, rearranging products for efficiency. The cashier speaks politely but with urgency, guiding the flow. The conveyor belt continues its steady rhythm, the machine's whirring a constant soundtrack. A receipt printer whirs to life, spitting out a slip of paper. The other shopper, now agitated, reaches around me to reach the front. 

Behind the glass, the cashier checks the last item, then moves on to the next one. The register chimes with confirmation, and the total is announced. Another beep signals a special offer, prompting the shopper to swipe their card. The conveyor belt pauses briefly, then resumes. The other customer, still pushing past, nearly collides with me. 

A momentary pause, then the scanner starts up again, the belt moving smoothly once more. The cashier, efficient as ever, finishes up the transaction. The register announces the final amount, and the loyalty-card prompt reappears. The conveyor belt slows to a stop, then restarts, the cycle continuing unabated. A receipt is handed over, and the shopper moves off, leaving the line momentarily empty. 

The cashier, now turning to face the next customer, prepares the scale, ready for the next item. The conveyor belt hums softly, the scanner ready for action. The divider bar remains in place, maintaining order. The other customer, now at the register, hands over their card, and the total is displayed. Beeps and whirs fill the air, the register working diligently. The line continues to move, the routine of retail seamlessly maintained.
